object_entity.proposition_label: The Son is eternally begotten from the Father
object_entity.description: The Son/Logos is not a creature brought into being at a point in time but is eternally generated from the substance of the Father — there was never a time when the Son was not. Key Origenian contribution that became foundational for Nicene orthodoxy.

evidence.notes: Light-brightness analogy for eternal generation.

passage.excerpt: The Son is the brightness of the eternal light. If this is so, then the Son is eternally begotten. For as brightness is generated from light without any interval, so also the Son is generated from the Father without any interval.
passage.notes: Eternal generation illustrated by the analogy of light and its brightness

evidence.notes: Explicit argument that the Father always generated the Son.

passage.notes: Free will as foundational church teaching; rational souls possess genuine freedom

evidence.notes: Explicit teaching on pre-existence of souls.

passage.notes: Pre-existence of souls and the explanation of different conditions through prior free will
